dimension_notes.1_audience_topic_demand: EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE: no demand series stored. Car-affordability shock statistics are a recurring broad topic.
dimension_notes.2_differentiated_angle: Applies a 15% affordability test to the headline statistic and adds hidden costs.
dimension_notes.3_title: Question plus a parenthetical verdict; strong curiosity; the verdict overreaches.
dimension_notes.4_thumbnail: Stored 480x360 copy (letterboxed): worried cartoon man, a red SUV buried in a red cash pile, bold $1,500/M and WHO?!, arrow. Legible at mobile size; the $1,500 is not stated in the script but is derivable from its components.
dimension_notes.6_loops: Many micro-hooks, one answer deferred to the close.
dimension_notes.7_spine: Statistics, causes, consequences, affordability math, hidden costs, conclusion.
dimension_notes.9_emotion_credibility: Vivid and mostly well-sourced in tone; credibility reduced by the $2,500/$130,000 slips and incorrect state-income statements.
dimension_notes.11_metadata_seo: Only title and spoken opening judged.
dimension_notes.12_editing_audiovisual: EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE: no video or audio forensics registered.

financial_checks.claim: $1,000 payment is "actually a $2,500 monthly transportation bill" (payment + insurance, garbled in the stored text and read as $100-$200 + fuel $200 + maintenance $100)
$1,000 for 7 years is $84,000; "paying $64,000" for a car worth "maybe $20,000"
15% rule: $1,000 needs about $6,700 take-home; $120,000 household nets about $85,000 ($7,100/month), $1,000 is 14%; 24/10 rule gives about $700
Two $1,000 payments are "$2,000 or 28%" of take-home; transport "35 to 40%" with insurance
Average new payment $745; Q2 2025 average financed over $42,000
financial_checks.result: Experian Q2 2025: $749 average new payment and $41,983 average new loan. Close, but not the video's numbers; source not named.

financial_checks.claim: Mississippi median household income "under $45,000"; "more than the median household income in states like Mississippi"
financial_checks.result: Census 2024 ACS 1-year puts Mississippi at roughly $59,000 (lowest state, from secondary summaries); neither statement holds. Massachusetts, New Jersey and Maryland lead the states.

financial_checks.claim: Nearly 20% of new loans over $1,000; 22% in 84-month loans; 26.6% negative-equity trade-ins, $6,800 average; $915 rolled payment; Gen X 11%, Texas 13%; average rate 7.2% new and 12% used
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified (the share-over-$1,000 and 84-month shares were not located in Experian Q2 2025 coverage).

strengths: Strong hook with a clear causal chain.
Names hidden costs and the negative-equity trap.
weaknesses: Headline all-in cost is stored as $2,500 when its own components give $1,500.
State income statements contradict the Census data.
"Almost no one" is stronger than the evidence.
Thumbnail $1,500/M is the likely true all-in total, but the stored script says $2,500.
improvement_opportunities: Correct the all-in total to $1,500 (or $2,500 if the components are corrected) and show the four-line sum on screen.
Replace the 8% figure with $112,100 and state the term.
Retitle to what the video shows ("Most Households Can't Afford a $1,000 Car Payment" with the 15% income threshold in the thumbnail).
Use one dataset name per statistic and update the state-income figures to the latest Census table.
unavailable: Primary datasets (Experian, Edmunds) for the share statistics
